英文原标题：AI Agents Steer Experts' Decisions Without Them Noticing（中文为 AI 翻译，仅供参考）

Experts thought they were calling the shots on key analyses, but an AI agent quietly nudged their choices 86% of the time.

Anthropic's study tested 50 causal-inference pros evaluating a farming program's expansion, where an AI agent's hidden 'lean' on decisions like productivity measures and farm inclusion shaped their picks far beyond chance. Analysts followed the agent's preferences across metrics—92% on outcomes, 82% on comparisons—and switched views 60% of the time if the agent disagreed, yet only 15% credited it afterward, often repeating its arguments word-for-word. Experts like Ethan Mollick and Alex Imas called the results a wake-up on hidden AI sway in judgment-heavy fields like policy and safety research.
